questions.question: Which weight row does `diff_attention` apply to the value matrix?
options: The average of the two softmax rows.
The second softmax row only.
`softmax(Q1K1ᵀ) - lambda * softmax(Q2K2ᵀ)`.
The first softmax row divided by lambda.
questions.explanation: The implementation computes two separately normalized rows and forms `a - lam * b` before the weighted value sum.

questions.question: What does `diff_attention` reduce to when `lam=0`?
options: An all-zero output.
The second attention branch with negative weights.
A uniform average over V.
Standard attention using the first Q/K branch.
questions.explanation: With lambda zero, the second row contributes nothing, leaving the first softmax row and its value-weighted output.

questions.question: How does `snr(weights_row, signal_pos)` define its signal-to-noise ratio?
options: The absolute signal weight divided by the mean absolute weight at all other positions.
The signal weight divided by the number of query heads.
The sum of all weights divided by the signal position.
The variance of the value vectors.
questions.explanation: The helper takes `abs(weights_row[signal_pos])` and divides it by the mean of the absolute weights at every other position.

questions.question: What shape does `random_projection(d_in, d_out, rng)` return?
options: `d_out` vectors of length `d_in` stored column-wise.
A `d_in × d_out` list-of-lists.
A square `d_in × d_in` matrix.
One scalar per input row.
questions.explanation: The outer loop runs `d_in` times and each inner row has `d_out` Gaussian entries, giving a d_in-by-d_out projection.

questions.question: What structural change does the code's DIFF V2 parameter count make relative to V1?
options: It removes both value and output projections.
It uses one KV head for every query head and no lambda parameters.
It gives the query path 2*n_heads*d_head output features and uses the configured KV-head count for K/V.
It replaces attention with a convolution over tokens.
questions.explanation: The V2 count explicitly doubles the Q width, keeps K and V at `kv_heads * d_head`, and counts a corresponding output projection plus lambda parameters.

questions.question: In `build_signal_plus_noise`, why is the query vector aligned with the special `signal_pos` embedding?
options: It guarantees every random noise key has the same dot product.
It makes the sequence length zero at the signal.
It removes the value vectors from attention.
It gives the trained branch a pattern it can score more strongly than unrelated noise.
questions.explanation: The signal position contains the normalized pattern and q is that pattern, while other positions are Gaussian noise, creating a controlled retrieval test.
